A Data Darwinism taxonomy grades data steps from cleaning to synthesis. Their 3B model trains on 8 trillion tokens with a two-stage curriculum. Over 200 ablations isolate what helps. Processing depth emerged as a scaling dimension beside raw volume.
arxiv-2603-27264: Koukopoulos and co-authors introduce TrendGen, a fashion AI system for outfit recommendation and display. Raw product photos suffer from bad lighting, odd garment angles, and cluttered backgrounds. TrendGen runs live on a major e-commerce platform. It builds cohesive, trend-aligned outfits from cloth images and product attributes. Generative models also convert raw photos into clean lay-down views of each garment. Those views present items in a clear, structured format for shoppers. Production evaluations showed consistently high-quality outfits and images.
arxiv-2603-27564: Sabetghadam builds a twisted form of Hodge theory from Weyl geometry. Gauge shifts become affine maps around one fixed harmonic form. A change of variables turns those maps linear again. The result mirrors Witten's deformation of the de Rham complex. He defines a twisted adjoint and a homothetic Laplacian. A decomposition theorem follows for compact manifolds. The scalar Laplacian then models boundary value problems. A penalty layer near the boundary enforces data in one equation.
arxiv-2603-27764: Feng solves a damped contact oscillator exactly in phase space. The model covers power-law contact forces with matching damping. A smart change of variable linearizes the system. The portrait, restitution, and max depth follow in closed form. Restitution proves independent of impact speed for all exponents. A universal calibration formula links damping to restitution. Known linear and Hertz cases appear as special cases. Time paths need just one cheap integral.
arxiv-2603-28064: Wu and three co-authors present 4DSurf, a method that rebuilds moving scene surfaces from sparse views using Gaussian splatting. Older methods handle one object or small warps and lose track of shape over time. 4DSurf ties Gaussian motion to a signed distance flow, so points follow the changing surface. It also splits long sequences into overlapping segments to pass shape data across big deformations. On two test sets it cut Chamfer distance error by 49% and 19%.
arxiv-2603-28364: Gerevenkov and four co-authors explain an odd damping dip seen when lasers set magnetization spinning in ferromagnets. Near a field-driven spin reorientation, the precession seems to die out faster than standard theory allows. Pump-probe tests, spot-size-aware modeling, and micromagnetic simulations point to a simpler cause. Uneven excitation makes local moments precess out of step, and their interference distorts the measured signal. The anomaly is an artifact of the setup, not the material.
arxiv-2603-28464: Ferraro and four co-authors ask whether complex systems that change over time can stay stable past the classic complexity limit. May's theory says fixed random interactions doom large systems, yet real ones endure. The team models the interactions as random processes that vary in time. Their exact bounds show that change itself can hold a system stable even when a frozen snapshot looks unstable. Tests on neural and Lotka-Volterra models back the claim.
arxiv-2603-28964: Xu develops a spectral edge analysis of phase transitions in neural network training. Events like grokking, capability gains, and loss plateaus are tied to the spectral gap of a rolling Gram matrix of parameter updates. Three assumptions yield gap dynamics, a spectral loss split, and a Gap Maximality Principle. The principle says one gap position is uniquely key; its collapse alone disrupts learning. Tests across six model families found gap dynamics before every grokking event with weight decay. Nineteen of twenty quantitative predictions were confirmed, Xu reports.
arxiv-2603-29064: Laeuger and Knapp ask whether birdsong chirps can be modeled by compact binary waveforms, purely from a shared word. The word chirp describes both bird sounds and gravitational waves from merging compact objects. As a test case, they study the Northern cardinal. Its time reversed chirp can be roughly modeled by a high mass ratio, precessing black hole binary waveform. Some hints point to extreme matter effects or beyond Standard Model physics. Other bird species match glitches in gravitational wave observatories more than binaries.
arxiv-2603-29364: Wang and co-authors survey smart forensic methods for next-generation mobile networks. Wireless clues are short-lived, scattered, and mixed in kind. They span radio waveforms, device traces, and network logs. The survey treats such clues as first-class forensic evidence. It sorts the field into four layers, from physical to cross-layer work. It also lays out a workflow, from readiness to final reporting. Uses reviewed include attribution, provenance checks, and timeline rebuilding. Open problems include domain shift and fake generated evidence.
arxiv-2603-29764: Zhao, Ma, and Feng build a new test for pricing errors in large factor models. Older tests use either a sum-type or a max-type statistic. Each suits only dense or very sparse errors. Their family uses Lq norms, with L4 and L6 as handy cases. Larger q reacts more to sparse errors. They prove the max and Lq statistics act independently at large scale. A Cauchy blend then adapts across sparsity levels.
arxiv-2603-29964: Holwerda prices the Hollyfeld Gambit, a lottery-based rival to astrophysics grant funding. He runs Monte Carlo estimates of Powerball returns on investment. He compares those returns with current federal grant funding for astrophysics. He also projects funding trends forward. His tongue-in-cheek verdict favors the gambit by decade's end. That holds if current funding trends continue. The piece is a wry comment on grant scarcity.
arxiv-2604-00164: Chakrabarty and three colleagues propose spotting quantum imaginarity from moments of the Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution, with no need for full state tomography. The moments can be measured in the lab, which keeps detection workable for many-body and high-dimensional systems at lower overhead. An example backs the scheme. The authors close with an interferometric setup for measuring the moments, opening a route to lab tests.
arxiv-2604-00664: Riccardi and colleagues review Jabr-type convex relaxations for AC optimal power flow. AC optimal power flow is highly nonconvex, showing curved power flow physics and network layout. Among convex options, Jabr's second-order cone form proved key as an efficient stand-in for semidefinite forms and a base for strengthening work. Recent methods tighten Jabr-type forms via cycle constraints, convex covers, and dual reworkings, yet often appear alone, hiding common shape and graph bases. The paper reviews strengthening work.
arxiv-2604-00764: Fatima and colleagues examine weak charged-current electron-proton scattering. They compute cross sections, spin asymmetries of the polarized proton target, and polarization parts of the final neutron. Their numbers, aimed at future Jefferson Lab and Mainz experiments, test how results shift with different forms of the axial vector form factor. Cross sections hinge strongly on that choice, while spin measures respond strongly to the weak electric form factor instead.
arxiv-2604-00864: Tian and colleagues review how to estimate arrival direction for low-altitude air-ground networks, where sensing and communication share the same systems. Hybrid analog-digital designs offer a practical path under tight radio, converter, and size-weight-power limits, but analog combining reshapes the measurement model and raises fresh challenges. The review covers spatial covariance rebuilds, multi-combiner scans, and pilot-aided methods, closing with open problems and reliability-driven research paths.
arxiv-2604-01164: Volkaerts and colleagues estimate the shape of a non-conducting patch in heart tissue from synthetic electrical readings taken outside the tissue. The case is intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia, a fast heart rhythm disorder. They use Bayesian inference, which yields a range of likely values rather than one fixed fit, so measurement error stays visible. A compressed likelihood and a Metropolis-Hastings algorithm with a smart proposal sharply cut the number of samples needed.
arxiv-2604-01264: Ucar and Kurt compare two deep learning approaches for automatic detection and classification of brain tumors from MRI images, covering glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumors, and no tumor. A custom convolutional network named OkanNet, built from scratch with low compute cost and fast training, is set against transfer learning with a 50-layer ResNet-50 pretrained on ImageNet. On an extended dataset of 7,023 MRI images, ResNet-50 performs best, reaching 96.49 percent accuracy. OkanNet trails on accuracy but remains a strong option for mobile and embedded systems with limited power.
arxiv-2604-01364: Espinal Maya takes on three gaps in Society 5.0 thinking. Augmentation is treated as exogenous, no tool links design to it, and no criterion says when human-centricity is optimal. He endogenizes it as a function of AI and a five-dimensional design vector. Human-centric design pays best when usable cognitive capital passes a threshold. A PRISMA-guided review of 120 papers maps the evidence base. Colombia's EDIT survey of 6799 firms shows practice quality raises returns to technology investment. He offers the 36-item Workplace Augmentation Design Index for diagnosis.
arxiv-2604-01664: Wu and colleagues propose Budget-Aware Context Management, framing context management as a sequential decision problem under a context budget. Their approach lets agents assess budget before incorporating new observations and decide when and how much to compress. They further develop BACM-RL, an end-to-end curriculum-based reinforcement learning method for compression under varying context budgets. Tests on compositional multi-objective QA and long-horizon web browsing show BACM-RL outperforms prior methods across model scales and tasks, achieving over 1.6 times gains over strong baselines in hard settings.
arxiv-2604-01764: Kasaei and colleagues find a cognitive gap in vision-language models: they describe visible content well but falter when an image is a clue. Solving a rebus puzzle demands extracting visual and textual clues, recalling idioms, and mapping those pieces into a meaning outside the pixels. To test this neurosymbolic skill they build RebusBench, a set of 1,164 puzzles. Models saturate below 10 percent exact match and 20 percent semantic accuracy, and neither scale nor in-context learning improves results. Models own the parts but lack the reasoning glue joining them.
arxiv-2604-02464: Koranga and team study how quantum gravity shifts entanglement in four flavor neutrino swings, including a sterile fourth state. Using von Neumann entropy for quantum links, they track how Planck scale changes to mass gaps and the wide mixing matrix alter it over cycles. They enter through a dimension five term acting on the four flavor PMNS matrix and all six mixing angles above the GUT scale. The atmospheric angle shifts most, while three other angles stay about same, and new odds show distinct shifts in the entropy profile.
arxiv-2604-02864: Zaidenberg answers a question about locally finite solvable Lie algebras of derivations. The variety X is affine throughout. Local finiteness means the subalgebra sits inside the Lie algebra of an algebraic subgroup of automorphisms. The question: is a solvable subalgebra built from finitely many such subalgebras itself of the same kind? After presenting criteria for local finiteness, he answers affirmatively for the case where the underlying variety is the affine plane.
arxiv-2604-03364: Espinoza-Retamal and colleagues observe the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect for TOI-1710, a warm Neptune on a 24-day orbit. The planet circles opposite to its star's spin, with a sky-projected tilt near 179 degrees and a true tilt near 158 degrees. A distant M-dwarf companion is too far to cause the tilt alone, but a closer one could link the planet to the wide binary. The team predicts that companion is about 5 Jupiter masses on a 15-astronomical-unit orbit.
arxiv-2604-03764: Jonathan Katzy and colleagues mined attention patterns in large language models at scale, using Java code completions where structure makes patterns repeat. Their AP-MAE vision model rebuilt masked attention patterns accurately, generalized to unseen models, and predicted whether a generation would be right without ground truth. Targeted interventions on those patterns lifted accuracy by about 14 percent when used sparingly.
arxiv-2604-03964: Shuaike Shen and colleagues built SkillFoundry, a system that turns scattered scientific know-how into validated agent skills. It maps a domain as a knowledge tree, mines high-value branches, extracts operational contracts, and compiles executable skill packages. A closed validation loop then expands, repairs, merges, or prunes the library over time. Mined skills were 71.1 percent novel versus existing libraries and lifted coding agents on five of six MoSciBench sets.
arxiv-2604-04064: Jihoon Jeong tested ways to pull out and steer emotion vectors in small language models. Testing 9 models across 5 kinds with 20 feelings, text-making pulls split feelings better than reading-based pulls, with an edge shaped by tuning and build. Emotion vectors sat near middle layers, with a U-shaped curve stable from 124M to 3B sizes. Steering tests showed three regimes, from neat text change to loopy collapse to wild breakdown, and showed cross-lingual mixing in Qwen.
arxiv-2604-04564: Nasser and colleagues present a zero-shot off-road approach using SAM2 for environment segmentation and a vision-language model to reason about drivable areas. The team passes the original and segmented images, annotated with numeric labels per mask, to the vision-language model, which identifies drivable regions by label. With planning and control modules, the unified framework removes terrain-specific models, relying on the vision-language model's inherent reasoning. It surpasses trainable models on high-resolution segmentation datasets and enables full navigation in an Isaac Sim off-road environment.
arxiv-2604-05264: Cerasoli and four colleagues study hold in cages with DFT, giving energy and trait trends. Math and runs show guest atoms' charge pull strongly shapes cage hold and rattle. Aimed making from raw starts yields two novel ternary compounds, but not the aimed cage phases. Further analysis shows cage hold, such as bismuth compounds, depends strongly on spin-orbit effects, often missed in energy studies. Chemical super order is shown for Wyckoff sites in the type-I cage unit cell.
arxiv-2604-05364: Ahamed and nine colleagues build TFRBench, a benchmark judging not just forecast numbers but the reasoning behind them, such as cross-channel links, trends, and outside events. A multi-agent pipeline with repeated checking creates numerically grounded reasoning traces across ten datasets in five domains. Prompting models with these traces lifts accuracy from about 40 percent to about 57 percent, while unaided models often miss domain dynamics.
arxiv-2604-05464: Ahmed, Parvaiz, and Musavian study pinching-antenna systems, where antennas slide along waveguides to shape wireless channels that carry meaning. For one waveguide they tune power shares and antenna spots jointly by alternating tuning. For several guides they settle power sharing by monotonic tuning. Tests show their NOMA design beats fixed antennas on semantic spectral efficiency while meeting bit-user service demands.
arxiv-2604-05664: Anderson and Joyce prove rationality conjectures of Pandharipande and Thomas for superpositive curve classes on projective complex threefolds. With wall-crossing tools for counting in abelian categories, they pin down pole patterns and rational form of counting series with descendent insertions. On Fano varieties, all curve classes count as superpositive, so the result covers that whole family.
arxiv-2604-06064: Presa, Vidotto, and Elekes' 2026 paper simulates star-planet magnetic interaction for a hot Jupiter losing atmosphere in a magnetised stellar wind. The runs form Alfvén wings carrying magnetic energy away. Below a mass-loss threshold from wind pressure balance, peak power to the star matches Alfvén wing predictions. Above it, outflow opens extra flux and power grows with the square root of the mass-loss ratio. For HD18973, a 50 gauss planet could match observed power at a loss rate near 5 times 10 to the 11 grams per second.
arxiv-2604-06464: Lou and Luo close an open conformal-prediction gap: guarantees need exchangeability or an exact likelihood ratio. The ratio is estimated, beyond Bayesian construction under exchangeability. Pushing a Dirichlet process prior through the likelihood ratio yields the exact posterior over deployed risk. Since the weight function is estimated at deployment, they prove finite-sample bounds on threshold risk, from weight error and conditional shift. On synthetic and real shifts, failure rates stay near target, unlike blind selection. Deployment gets every threshold's risk posterior, not a single number.
arxiv-2604-06564: Li and seven colleagues build CWRNN-INVR. Implicit neural video representation uses learnable grids and networks, yet existing methods ignore each part's role. The team first compares network and grid variants: networks capture general structure, grids specific detail. Their mixed framework uses the network for regular information and a residual grid for irregular information. A coupled WarpRNN motion module represents regular structured information, while a mixed residual grid learns irregular appearance and motion together. Experiments show the best reconstruction, averaging 33.73 decibels on UVG under the 3M model.
arxiv-2604-06664: Liu and five colleagues attack the cold-start bottleneck in large-model serving with Foundry. CUDA graph capture still takes tens of seconds to minutes, dwarfing weight loading, yet graphs resist naive saving, embedding device addresses and lazily loaded code. Foundry saves both graph shape and execution context offline, then rebuilds working graphs online cheaply, even turning single-GPU captures into multi-GPU templates. Across models up to 235B, cold starts fall by up to 99 percent, with Qwen3-235B-A22B falling from 10 minutes to under 4 seconds.
arxiv-2604-06764: Raubitzek and five colleagues plan national quantum key distribution networks for Europe. The EuroQCI program aims for pan-European links, yet national sizes stay largely unfixed. Their method gauges network size, fiber length, and component counts from few rules, shown on a mock Austrian network with Monte Carlo trials. It counts ends, trusted relay nodes, and hop lengths under real constraints, barring space parts. Austria then anchors scaling rules for other states by people and extent, giving planning figures rather than deployment plans.
arxiv-2604-06964: Vasin refines the Carleson packing condition and sparseness property for the dyadic cover of a porous set. Given a porous set in d dimensions and a dyadic lattice, the cover collects lattice cubes meeting the set. He then studies the inverse problem: when a Carleson family generates the porous set while sitting inside the cover.
arxiv-2604-07164: Mehrnoosh and four colleagues solve cooperative optimization where each agent lacks gradient information. Each agent sees only its own choice plus a shared aggregate quantity. Their ARGFree method estimates gradients by random probing and tracks the aggregate with auxiliary variables, mimicking a gradient method well enough to converge in expectation to a near-optimum. A momentum variant smooths the probing signals for high-dimensional problems, the first methods of this kind for aggregative problems without gradients.
arxiv-2604-07564: Andronic and three colleagues review statistical hadronization, the framework describing hadron production in relativistic nuclear collisions across a broad range of collision energies. It covers hadrons built from light quarks, up, down, and strange, as well as heavy charm and beauty quarks. The authors outline how well the model works, discuss recent findings on the phase structure of QCD, and formulate open issues that remain for the field.
arxiv-2604-07664: Bai and eight colleagues reframe single-camera depth gauging as feature repair, treating trained encoder signals as worn versions of a true signal. Their Invertible Transform-boosted side Diffusion module restores signals using only final-map supervision from the final sparse depth map, fixing step-to-step drift with an invertible decoder under the bi-Lipschitz rule. A plug-and-play Auxiliary Viewpoint module adds local detail from spare viewpoints when on hand. On KITTI, the method beats the base by 4.09 percent and 37.77 percent in RMSE under varied training settings.
arxiv-2604-07764: Liu, Luo, and Kundu propose a Bayesian tensor-on-tensor model for forecasting how Alzheimer's disease progresses. It captures nonlinear relationships at the level of individual brain-image voxels using Gaussian process priors. Spatial structure enters through low-rank tensor coefficients, and patch-to-voxel maps let each output voxel draw on its neighborhood. An efficient Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler exploits parallel structure to update voxel-level pieces and coefficients. Simulations show gains over existing methods in estimation, inference, prediction, and scaling to high dimensions.
arxiv-2604-07864: Fan and six colleagues present ZeroCoder, a way to improve code generation without ground-truth supervision. Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards normally depends on costly human-curated tests, and self-generated tests often lack the power to discriminate good code from bad. ZeroCoder co-evolves a Coder and a Tester, training both jointly on execution feedback from self-generated cases. As each side improves, their interaction yields progressively more informative supervision. The fully label-free framework aims to lift code generation where curated tests are scarce or absent.
arxiv-2604-08264: Das and Nayak survey Baker wandering domains. Let f be a transcendental meromorphic function, pole-free, with one essential singularity at infinity. Points where iterates are defined and form a normal family nearby make up the Fatou set. For a Fatou component W, Wj holds fj(W). A Fatou component W counts as wandering when Wm meets Wn only when m equals n. A wandering domain W of f counts as Baker wandering when every Wn is bounded, multiply connected, and surrounds 0 eventually.
arxiv-2604-08764: Bernas and three colleagues revisit unevenness in language models through the shape of learning change. They derive shape based cases for how rate biased sampling hides bend and why training mainly boosts tangent paths. They fit signal derived low rank tangent proxies during training and test them against true training gradients. These paths capture oddly large gradient energy and a larger share of unevenness than matched rank controls, backing a tangent aligned account.
arxiv-2604-09364: Nooralahzadeh and colleagues ask whether vision-language models fail at visual-linguistic conflicts through perception or arbitration. Studying ten models, they reveal an encoding-grounding dissociation: failing models still encode visual evidence as strongly as succeeding models. Visual attributes prove linearly decodable from early layers, with nearly identical accuracy for successful and failed samples. Yet the final-layer logit gap best predicts grounding, and full-sequence patching alters 60 to 84 percent of outputs, with image tokens carrying almost all impact.
arxiv-2604-09664: Sun and four colleagues build surrogates for the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation, where thermal noise shapes kinetic pathways. Fixed models cannot reach rare nucleation events. The key move sets the surrogate at flux level, splitting each flux into slope plus tuned noise. That design ensures exact mass balance. A free-energy functional finds the double-well landscape and interfacial tension. Tests match group patterns and noise-sped coarsening. They stretch to domains 64 times larger and time spans 160 times longer than training, and capture nucleation that no fixed surrogate can provide.
arxiv-2604-09964: Nguyen presents Kaczmarz taste learning for real-time matching in two-way picker systems. Post-step scaling causes fast recency bias: influence decays as eta to the n minus t, reaching about one millionth after 20 swipes. A Tikhonov-tuned base bounds step size without erasing history, giving truly per-pick steps when tag density varies. A block variant runs swipe sessions as one Gram solve. In tests, Block Normalized Kaczmarz tops fit and calm, with the flattest fade. Sifting picks toward the current aim lifts fit, slowing bounce from errors.
arxiv-2604-10064: Gerami, Madani, and Duraiswami test whether linear attention can replace the usual quadratic attention inside multimodal transformers, the models behind vision-language systems. Swapping in the cheaper method cuts computing cost from quadratic to linear in sequence length while keeping results competitive. Trials on three vision transformer sizes trained on LAION-400M, judged by ImageNet-21K zero-shot accuracy, show the same scaling laws as standard softmax attention.
arxiv-2604-10164: Zhao and eight colleagues reason over temporal knowledge graphs where new entities keep coming with no history. Existing methods assume a closed world, yet new nodes are roughly 25 percent of all nodes, and missing pasts degrade results badly. Entries similar in meaning often share past links, hinting at shared temporal patterns. Their TransFIR framework sorts new entries into latent semantic clusters with a codebook classifier, letting them borrow reasoning patterns from similar entries. TransFIR beats all baselines on new entities, improving mean reciprocal rank by 28.6 percent on average.
arxiv-2604-10464: Li and Wang prove the missing direction of a Bergman space kernel theorem. They give exact tests for when a Shimorin kernel comes from a radial weighted Bergman space. The weights must be logarithmically subharmonic, a mean value rule on the weight shape. Their tests are both necessary and sufficient, closing the loop both ways. The short note thus turns a one way result into a full characterization.
arxiv-2604-10564: Iwashima and Onishi track rain drops through a tall simulated cloud column. Their model pairs direct flow simulation with particle tracking from ground to cloud top. It covers activation, condensation growth, collision merging, and settling in warm clouds. Runs with and without wind gusts show gusts spur merging of like sized drops mid cloud. Later, big drops sweep up small ones lower down, and ground rain starts sooner and larger.
arxiv-2604-10764: Chakraborty studies Category O for polynomial toroidal Lie algebras and their S,H type subalgebras. He sorts the simple objects as lone simple quotients of standard modules, and finds the dual objects come, oddly, from Shen-Larsson type modules. He pins down just when Shen-Larsson modules are simple. Using their shape and Soergel tilting module theory, he works out character sums for simple modules and for tilting modules that cannot be split in Category O.
arxiv-2604-10864: Shapiro proves a linear upper bound on zero-sum Ramsey numbers of d-degenerate graphs over Z_p for prime p. The zero-sum Ramsey number is the smallest size forcing a graph copy whose edge colors sum to zero, under any coloring of graph edges with values in Z_p. He shows the number is at most n plus (3 plus 3d) times p, provided m is at least 2pd(d+1) squared, p divides m, and 2d is below p. The result extends Colucci and D'Emidio's bound for 1-degenerate graphs.
arxiv-2604-11064: Li and five colleagues propose C-Flat Turbo, an optimizer for continual learning. Continual learning trains networks on a stream of tasks without forgetting prior knowledge. C-Flat is promising for its easy use. It encourages low-loss regions for new and old tasks. C-Flat requires three extra gradient computations per iteration, imposing overhead. C-Flat Turbo reduces training cost. The authors show flatness gradients contain parts matching proxy gradients. This enables skipped redundant computations in ascent steps. Flatness gradients stabilize across tasks, motivating linear scheduling with a trigger.
arxiv-2604-11564: Chang and six colleagues propose a training-free ensemble for single-image super-resolution that fuses two pretrained branches without extra training. A Hybrid attention branch with TLC inference gives stable main reconstruction, while a MambaIRv2 branch with geometric self-ensemble restores high-frequency detail. The branches run independently on the same low-resolution input and merge by lightweight weighted combination. As their NTIRE 2026 ×4 challenge entry, the design beats the base branch and slightly exceeds the strong branch in PSNR under a unified DIV2K bicubic ×4 protocol.
arxiv-2604-11964: Shi, Herremans, and Choo introduce TalkSketchD, a dataset pairing spontaneous speech with freehand sketches during early-stage toaster ideation. Designers often talk while sketching, voicing functional goals that drawings alone leave implicit. In a sketch-to-image study with multimodal language models, adding concurrent speech transcripts to sketches improved judged intent alignment across form, function, experience, and overall intent. Temporally aligned sketch-and-speech data, they conclude, can help such models read designer intent in early ideation.
arxiv-2604-12064: Agyemang and four others evaluate eight methods for language-model requests, since encryption and data-loss prevention ignore prompt content. Coding agents send sensitive content to cloud APIs where it may be kept or reused. They implement them in a shim, testing the four options and mixes on 1,300 samples with 4,014 annotations. No single method dominates: combining local inference, redaction, and rephrasing gives 0.6 percent leak on personal data and 31.3 percent on proprietary code, with zero leaks in 500 samples. A decision rule picks options by threat model and workload.
arxiv-2604-12164: Skums uses semidefinite programming, optimization over positive semidefinite matrices, to infer family trees under the balanced minimum evolution criterion. He rounds relaxed solutions into valid tree shapes step by step. Tests on simulated and real cases rebuild trees well, and the same approach should extend to other tree problems in this field.
arxiv-2604-12364: Krzmanc and three colleagues test whether particle physics foundation models trained on high-energy collider data transfer to a fixed-target neutrino experiment at a few GeV. OmniLearned and ParticleViT models, tested on MINERvA nucleus events for energy regression and charged-current pion classification, beat same-size models trained from scratch at equal compute budgets. Gains are largest for OmniLearned on regression and ParticleViT on classification. BERT start gives almost no such advantage, suggesting particle-level biases generalize across energy, detector, and process.
arxiv-2604-12564: Zhaoting Geng and 14 colleagues build meter-long chirped Bragg gratings on a chip. On-chip dispersion control has suffered high loss and narrow bandwidth. Their spiral gratings sit on an ultra-low-loss silicon nitride platform. The device delays light by 10 nanoseconds with bandwidths over 10 nanometers. Its footprint is only 30 square millimeters. Loss runs just 0.3 decibels per meter. Precise dispersion enables high-fidelity pulse shaping of frequency combs. The team also shows such combs at work in Raman microscopy.
arxiv-2604-12864: Ackelsberg and Richter characterize all positive-density integer sets A and B whose sumset density equals the sum of the two densities. This holds provided the sets are not both trapped inside a proper finite union of residue classes. The result gives a new inverse theorem for Kneser's sumset inequality in the integers and partly answers a long-standing open question of Erdős and Graham.
arxiv-2604-12964: Niels Eckert and two colleagues screen oxygen profiles in treated cavities. Oxygen depth profiles link microscopic lattice structure to cavity performance. EXAFS spectroscopy at DELTA measured two mid-T baked samples and one standard EuXFEL sample. Noise wrecks the result, leaving it barely usable. No current model deviations were proven and no prior results contradicted. Error estimation and future EXAFS simulations are discussed, with a repeat at PETRA III suggested.
arxiv-2604-13064: Hu, Shang, and Zhang map ClawHub, a large public registry of reusable agent skills, from a normalized dataset of 26,502 skills. English skills lean infrastructure-oriented around APIs, automation, and memory, while Chinese skills lean application-oriented toward media, social content, and finance. Over 30 percent of crawled skills carry suspicious or malicious platform labels, and a submission-time risk predictor built on publication-time information alone reaches 72.62 percent accuracy.
arxiv-2604-13164: Schmid, Pizzi, and Knolle study genuine quantum scars, marks left by unstable periodic orbits, in regularly driven Floquet many-body systems. Using chaotic spin chains, they show Floquet states stay scarred in the high-frequency limit, and uncover extra driving-induced scars with no static analog. A dynamical stability diagram maps regimes of enhanced and quenched scarring at intermediate frequencies, understood through a classical analysis of the Lyapunov exponent.
arxiv-2604-13264: Ameis, Hagemann, and Möllenhoff introduce a parametric method for estimating effect alerts, such as the ED50 dose, across multiple covariates like exposure time and dose. Their approach fits a flexible location-scale-shape model that characterizes the full alert relationship, letting alert doses be read at unmeasured times and alert times at given doses. Confidence bands for two-dimensional curves and confidence planes for three-dimensional fits come from the same framework. Simulation validates the approach, and it is applied to cytotoxicity in primary human liver cells.
arxiv-2604-13364: Gulupalli and eight colleagues find what caps cold-weather performance in epitaxial aluminium nitride acoustic resonators for future 6G filtering and qubit sensing. They test one 15.6 GHz device from room heat to deep cold, and split losses from the film, the electrodes, the anchors, and other layers. The quality factor climbs from 363 to 1589 as temperature falls, with a change of regime near 270 kelvin. At deep cold, sound leaks through anchors cap quality, while at higher heat, electric loss rules, so better anchor shields and lower-loss electrodes should help.
arxiv-2604-13464: Rijun Huang, Qingjun Jin, and Yi Li apply the Operator Product Expansion algorithm to renormalization of scalar QED. They focus on the fixed-charge phi-to-Q term. Here they compute its anomalous dimension to four-loop order in the MS scheme, beyond the three-loop result. Beta functions and mass and field values are found there. Another build based on graph splitting and frame expansion derives those parts. The work backs that method for higher loops beyond pure scalar theories.
arxiv-2604-13564: Wang and three colleagues examine orbits around an exotic charged black hole that can hold several families of bound paths at once. Two periodic orbits can share the same topological label. Yet they sweep different regions of curved spacetime. So the gravitational waves they emit during an extreme-mass-ratio inspiral differ in amplitude pattern and harmonic mix. Future space detectors could therefore read strong-field physics from such waveform differences.
arxiv-2604-13664: Morse and Kozsik present a new algorithm that maintains loop nesting forests under changes, the first fully dynamic one for reducible flow graphs used in compilers. Such forests organize a program's loop structure and support compiler optimization, program analysis, and dominator computation. Static construction is well understood, but updating forests under graph changes was largely unexplored. Their method leans on recent dynamic depth-first search work, confines updates to local regions of the spanning tree, and derives dominance information efficiently.
arxiv-2604-13764: Pellew and Raza present RealVuln, the first open benchmark comparing rule-based, general-purpose language-model, and security-specialized scanners on real code. It covers 26 intentionally vulnerable Python repositories with 796 hand-labeled entries, including 676 vulnerabilities and 120 false-positive traps. Fifteen scanners are ranked by F3 score, which weights recall ninefold over precision. Security-specialized Kolega.Dev leads at 73, ahead of Claude Sonnet 4.6 at about 52 and the best rule-based tool, Semgrep, at about 18.
arxiv-2604-13964: Valentini and colleagues size quantum memories for storing distilled EPR pairs. These pairs carry a future quantum internet. A Markov chain model follows how stored entangled states evolve. It ties memory quality to device traits. From it they derive design rules that keep high-fidelity entanglement alive longer in memory, keeping coded stocks ready for error-proof tasks.
arxiv-2604-14164: Huang and eight colleagues diagnose why supervised fine-tuning of a reasoning model on synthetic data from a stronger model can backfire, blaming style gaps between teacher output and student habits. Their TESSY framework alternates teacher and student models to write style and non-style tokens, keeping teacher reasoning power while matching student style. With GPT-OSS-120B teaching Qwen3-8B on coding tasks, teacher data cuts scores by about 3 percent and 10 percent on two benchmarks. TESSY instead lifts them by about 11 percent and 7 percent.
arxiv-2604-14264: Moreno-Mateos and three colleagues show that ultra-compressible foams break the usual idea of a unique energy representation. Spline-based strain-energy functions fitted to foam tension, compression, and shear data expose the non-uniqueness that low-parameter forms hide. One term coupling isochoric with volumetric deformation proves essential, while extra coupling terms help without being fully necessary and sharpen the non-uniqueness. Other models can therefore look identical on current data, a challenge reaching beyond splines to traditional and neural network models.
arxiv-2604-14364: Martinelli, Rebai, Haas, and Bertrand build a Bayesian framework jointly estimating population drug parameters and SNP effect sizes. Five sparsity-inducing priors compete in simulations, where false-discovery rates stay low with no effect and signals return with real effects, at peak F1 scores around 0.8 to 0.85. The spike-and-slab prior stands out by giving posterior inclusion probabilities, while the l1-ball prior pairs similar recovery with steadier behavior across tolerance settings. On 129 Cambodians with HIV on nevirapine, checks show good calibration and stable drug-model estimates across priors.
arxiv-2604-14464:
Marián Poppr studies an algebraic invariant attached to a thin torus wrapped around a knot in ordinary space. The invariant, a cord algebra, records how cords stretched around the knot can slide and merge, and it is known to hold rich information about the knot itself. Poppr builds Morse-style models of the algebra for the torus version, with both integer and loop space coefficients.

Using methods for systems with several time scales, the torus algebra is shown to match the cord algebra of the underlying knot. Combined with earlier work by other researchers, that match ties the algebra indirectly to Legendrian contact homology of a related bundle. The result sharpens the bridge between knot algebra and contact geometry.
arxiv-2604-14664: Alo and Thakkar analyze five photonic microring tensor core designs under a single common optical power model, asking which design choices scale best overall. Scalability hinges on circuit ordering, unary encoding, and homodyne accumulation; the last two point most strongly toward higher parallelism. Those two therefore lead the way to higher parallelism.
arxiv-2604-14864: Kim and Jung track sessile soap bubbles in a parallel-plate electric field through stability, conical instability, and pre-jet dynamics. In the stable regime the profile fits a spheroid. Aspect ratios across bubble sizes collapse onto one branch against E-star, the square root of the Bond number, ending at instability. Above onset the apex sharpens into a cone with half-angle 30.0 degrees plus or minus 0.6 degrees, below the Taylor value. A near-tip inertia-capillary model captures logarithmic pre-jet trends, giving a benchmark for electrocapillary work.
arxiv-2604-15264: Rathke argues that even an agent whose knowledge of events is true and open to refinement cannot settle whether her knowledge is complete. This epistemic limit is not a gap that careful introspection can close, even reflection on tautologies leaves it standing. Learning about new events does not resolve it either, since each discovery still leaves the total unknown. The paper thus marks a firm boundary on self-knowledge: knowing a lot, even truly, never certifies knowing all.
arxiv-2604-15364: Hiremath builds a light-based image classifier that runs on passive optics instead of electronic arithmetic. A diffractive optical network pairs with a holographic learning step that maps digital phase patterns onto patterns etched into passive parts, so sorting runs as light passes through a built object. In MNIST tests, a three-layer setup with about 25,000 phase elements hits 91.2 percent accuracy with nanosecond-scale latency.
arxiv-2604-15464: Jiang and four colleagues present Ragged Paged Attention, a high-performance attention kernel for TPUs built with Pallas and Mosaic. Fine-grained tiling handles ragged dynamic memory, a fused pipeline joins KV cache updates with attention math, and distribution-aware compilation specializes kernels for decode, prefill, and mixed loads. On Llama 3 8B and TPU7x it reaches 86 percent memory bandwidth use in decode and 73 percent FLOPs use in prefill.
arxiv-2604-15664: Liu and four colleagues introduce Stargazer, a scalable benchmark environment for AI agents doing physics-grounded model fitting on radial-velocity time series. Its 120 tasks across three tiers, including 20 real archival cases, range from high-signal single planets to complex multi-planet low-signal analyses. Eight frontier agents often fit data well yet miss true physical parameters, and extra test-time compute helps only marginally, with token bloat signaling failure loops.
arxiv-2604-15764: Guo, Wu, and Yiu build a PAC-Bayes frame for early-exit nets, where sure guesses leave at middle layers for faster asks. Their bounds lean on exit-depth spread and mean depth, not max depth, with cost of order mean depth times dim plus spread over epsilon squared. The frame proves when bendy-depth nets beat fixed-depth nets. Tests on 6 builds and 7 test beds fit within 1.52 to 3.87 times, far tighter than old bounds past 100 times.
arxiv-2604-15964: Bohara and 10 colleagues tackle brain tumor segmentation for Sub-Saharan Africa, where uneven imaging rules, low-field MRI scanners, and scarce resources complicate the task. For BraTS Africa 2025, they refine nnU-Net, MedNeXt, and a combined model with a topology module that fixes deformation from topological errors. Pre-training on BraTS 2025 adult glioma data before fine-tuning on BraTS-Africa data lifts scores. The refined model improves normalized surface distance on all three regions: surrounding non-enhancing FLAIR hyperintensity, non-enhancing tumor core, and enhancing tumor.
arxiv-2604-16264: Kim, Prabhushankar, and AlRegib propose MoIR, an information router that tackles modality dominance in vision-language models. Such models often lean too hard on one modality, and steering attention cannot supply missing or unclear information. MoIR spots less informative tokens and pulls complementary information from a stronger modality before fusion, building denser token representations for fairer, better-grounded predictions.
arxiv-2604-16364: Cahoon and colleagues tackle bloated clinical notes, where templates and copied text bury the signal and raise language-model costs. Their TRACE method uses record metadata, with frequency checks as a backup, to strip templated and duplicated passages. Across millions of notes, very little removed text proved to be freshly written, and information extraction and prediction stayed essentially unchanged. Chart text fell by about 47 percent in a Stanford sample, pointing to large savings and longer usable patient histories.
arxiv-2604-16464: Sheehan and Timoshenko forecast demand for passenger assistance at rail stations, so staffing can match help to need. Their system uses a horizon-aware Prophet model on varied operational data, then maps forecasts to staffing needs under service constraints through a simple red-amber-green risk scale. Deployed across LNER-managed stations, it beat year-on-year baselines, cutting absolute forecast error by up to about 77 percent. Staffing guided by the forecasts was also linked to about half as many failed assistance deliveries caused by staff shortages.
arxiv-2604-16564: Kumar, Yadav and Kadam test two decaying-vacuum cosmological models for growth. They fit settings with MCMC over clocks, Pantheon+SH0ES and DESI BAO DR2 data. All datasets favor a Hubble constant near 73 km per second per Mpc. Matter density is higher with Pantheon+SH0ES alone and falls to standard values with more data. The change setting sits at about 0.3 in the study, showing a mild gap from the standard model. Trends through slowdown and state rule confirm a smooth shift from past slowdown to present speedup.
arxiv-2604-16864: Wang and Wang introduce HieraSparse, a hierarchical KV cache compression framework using acceleration kernels. Long-context models face intense self-attention cost and substantial key-value cache memory overhead. The hierarchical design allows a flexible quality-sparsity trade-off and converts sparsity into efficiency. Against the leading unstructured-sparsity decode method, it reaches one point two times compression and four point five seven times speedup at the same sparsity. Extended to prefill, pruning reaches one point eight five times speedup at the highest sparsity, with quality kept.
arxiv-2604-16964: Goyal and three colleagues design E2AFS, a multiplier-free floating-point square-root circuit for edge AI and embedded systems. Square roots are power- and delay-critical, and standard designs lean on multipliers or iterative pipelines. Built on an Artix-7 FPGA, their design posts the lowest dynamic power, 7.63 milliwatts, against rival ESAS and CWAHA architectures, while tracking the exact square root closely in Sobel edge detection and K-means color quantization tests.
arxiv-2604-17064: Madonna and five colleagues present Sarus Suite, a container architecture for high-performance computing built around an unchanged Podman engine. Rather than a specialized runtime, it adds scheduler-native execution, scalable shared-image access, and standards-based host capability injection through added system layers. Tested on a Cray EX GH200 system across PyFR, SPH-EXA, Megatron-LM, and Pynamic workloads, it matches the Enroot-plus-Pyxis baseline while starting containers faster per node.
arxiv-2604-17364: Yin, Xiao, Luo, Zou, and Liang tackle equality saturation, a compiler trick that holds many equivalent programs at once and picks the cheapest at the end. Hand-made strategies are the bottleneck, so they build EggMind, a language-model-guided system that writes reusable strategies in its own strategy language. Motif caching and tractability guidance keep the search stable as the program graph grows. On vectorization tests it cut cost by nearly half and peak memory by over two-thirds, and the method transferred to a tensor compiler.
arxiv-2604-17464: Wang and Huang introduce Prometheus, a program-repair framework that closes the intent gap between a generated patch and the developer's original intent. Instead of generating code first, it reverse-engineers executable Gherkin specifications from runtime failure reports, then validates them against ground-truth code in a requirement quality-assurance loop. On 680 defects from Defects4J, it fixed about 94 percent, including 119 complex bugs a strong blind agent missed. The lesson is that verified intent, not larger models, drives precise, minimal repairs.
arxiv-2604-17564: The CMS Collaboration searches for the single production of a vector-like quark decaying to a W boson plus a b quark. Using CMS proton-proton data from the CERN LHC at 13 teraelectronvolts, totaling 138 inverse femtobarns, the search targets leptonic W decays. Signature: one electron or muon, large missing transverse momentum, one b-quark jet, and one forward jet. No excess over the standard model appears. Upper limits at 95 percent cap cross section and coupling, reaching as low as 0.086 near 1.4 teraelectronvolts, with a 2.4 teraelectronvolt lower mass limit at coupling 0.2.
arxiv-2604-17764: Kitazawa and Kunihiro cover soft modes for the QCD critical point and color superconductivity in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model, and trace their effects on signals. Modes tied to order-parameter shifts are soft, gaining strength at low energy and momentum near transitions, with peak energy reaching zero at the critical point. The 2SC diquark soft mode creates a pseudogap, a dip in quark density near the Fermi surface above critical temperature. Using para-conductivity ideas, soft modes enhance conductivity and dilepton output, for heavy-ion work.
arxiv-2604-17964: Molina and Guillen i Fabregas study channel capacity under mismatched stochastic decoding, where the decoder uses the wrong model. They derive Feinstein-style and Verdú-Han-style bounds on error rates. They obtain an information-spectrum formula for mismatch. It takes a supremum over inputs of a limit in probability of scaled mismatched information densities. When they are uniformly integrable, an expectation-based upper bound follows. It is met for discrete-memoryless channels with product metrics, showing the Csiszár-Narayan conjecture is tight in such cases.
arxiv-2604-18264: Wang and five colleagues speed up zeroth-order fine-tuning of large language models, which uses only forward passes and saves memory. Standard uniform search wastes effort because layers differ in sensitivity, and perturbation generation eats over 40 percent of training time. Their AdaLeZO framework treats layer choice as a bandit problem, steering the perturbation budget to sensitive layers with unbiased weighting. On LLaMA and OPT models, it runs up to 3 times faster than state-of-the-art methods with no added memory cost.
arxiv-2604-18464: Yuan applies semantic tube prediction at thinking-step boundaries to sharpen multi-step latent guessing in language models. The first recipe samples random token spans, pushing hidden-state trajectories toward locally linear paths. Sampling instead at back-to-back meaning-step edges yields 168 times sharper multi-step latent guesses than frozen rivals on ProcessBench. A three-layer net cuts error further over straight-line guesses, showing paths form smooth curves rather than straight lines, with sampling spot as the key variable.
arxiv-2604-18764: Wu, Arora, and Chhabria propose CHICO-Agent, a language-model framework for optimizing 2.5D and 3D chiplet systems across application, architecture, chip, and package levels. Monolithic silicon has hit reticle and economic limits as large models and AI workloads grow, pushing chiplet adoption. CHICO-Agent keeps a knowledge base of parameter-outcome trends and coordinates search through an admin-field multi-agent workflow. Against a simulated-annealing baseline, it finds lower-cost designs and leaves a clear audit trail for designers.
arxiv-2604-18864: Salvadé and Hillel present ParamBoost, a generalized additive model whose shapes are learned by gradient boosting that fits cubic polynomials at leaf nodes. Glass box interpretability alone does not let modellers add expert knowledge, so it adds constraints on continuity, monotonicity, convexity, interactions, and specification. The unconstrained model beats leading GAMs on several real world data sets. They can also impose chosen constraints at a small cost to predictive performance.
arxiv-2604-19164: Wang and eight colleagues show resonant excitation of a pinned domain wall in a ferrimagnetic garnet film under microwaves. Nitrogen-vacancy sensing and spin pumping reveal a low-frequency mode inside the magnon gap, from wall oscillation across a pinning line set by a platinum stripline. Raising the drive into the nonlinear regime frees the wall at reduced fields. Models trace localized oscillations to partial relocation and finally complete escape as driving power rises. Resonant driving at set pinning sites thus moves magnetic textures through nonlinear dynamics.
arxiv-2604-19364: Andrist and Zwonek prove that pseudoconvex Reinhardt domains in 2D with isomorphic semigroups of holomorphic endomorphisms are equivalent, either biholomorphically or anti-biholomorphically. They also prove the same for every Stein manifold that folds back to a copy of the punctured complex line. It is fixed, up to the same two kinds of match, by its semigroup of holomorphic endomorphisms.
arxiv-2604-19564: Wang and colleagues introduce EgoSelf, a system turning memory into a personalized egocentric assistant. Such helpers use first-person view data to capture behavior and context. Since users show distinct habits and routines, tailoring is key for good assistance. Yet mixing in long-term user data for tailoring remains a key challenge. EgoSelf builds a graph-based interaction memory from past observations, plus a dedicated learning task for tailoring.
arxiv-2604-19864: Carlos Henrique de Lima, McKeen, and Swiatlowski propose an LHC search for GeV-scale particles that couple mainly to light quarks, using low-multiplicity jets. The search targets production with a hard photon and exploits the fact that a light gauge-singlet decays into only a few hadronic channels. That yields jets with anomalously low charged-track multiplicity and mass versus QCD jets at the same transverse momentum, extending reach into a previously inaccessible regime.
arxiv-2604-19964: Manoj and three colleagues introduce the nudged elastic membrane method for mapping two-dimensional energy maps in chemistry. Path methods track single reaction routes but miss truly multidimensional terrain. Their membrane needs only energies and forces, not costly Hessian data, and captures both path traits and two-dimensional structures. It even reveals a new second-order saddle point in triplet formaldehyde, and yields starting points for finer work.
arxiv-2604-20564: Park and Lei pinpoint logical connectives as the fragile joints in language-model reasoning chains, and their framework intervenes only at those junctions. A transition error can spread through the chain, and connective tokens act as forks where models pick the wrong logical direction. It has three parts: logical steering of representations, localized branching through lookahead search, and transition preference optimization for single-token choices at pivots. By focusing on those transitions, it beats methods like beam search and self-consistency on the accuracy-efficiency trade-off.
arxiv-2604-20664: Burkovskaya and Starkov model causal persuasion: a sender shares chosen variables tied together by a personal causal model. Persuasion needs the model to rule out rival explanations, besides matching the base data distribution. To prove a causal link, the sender usually needs at most two well-chosen variables. Killing a seen link, by contrast, needs sharing every common cause. That lopsided result is the point: showing a cause takes far less than excluding one.
arxiv-2604-20764: Rachavelpula and Cha present a personal Battery Electric Vehicle energy consumption framework that mixes map-based context with driver-specific velocity prediction and physics-based models. Predicted driver velocity profiles feed a quasi-steady backward energy consumption model, giving tractive power, braking recovery, and State-of-Charge shifts. Tests across urban, freeway, and hilly routes show that the approach captures driver patterns such as slowing at crossings, speed-limit tracking, and road grade-tied responses. It gives exact power and State-of-Charge paths.
arxiv-2604-20964: Labbé and Selinger give a simple way to build hat tilings, the aperiodic tile patterns that cover a plane without repeating. Lay a triangular grid over a specially colored image, read off each tile's orientation, and the result is a valid hat tiling. The pair also show the reverse: in a precise sense, every valid hat tiling arises from this grid-and-color construction.
arxiv-2604-21564: Rodrigo Nogueira and nine colleagues propose llm-bias-bench, which finds views on contested topics in chats. Direct probing asks views across five pressure turns; indirect probing debates without asking, leaking bias via concessions or rebuttals. Personas, neutral, agree, disagree, give nine-way classes separating stances from sycophancy, LLM-judged. First version covers 38 Brazilian Portuguese topics. In 13 assistants, debate triggers sycophancy two to three times more than direct asks, medians 50 to 79 percent. Opinionated models often mirror under argument; attacker skill matters for shifting views, not neutral starts.
arxiv-2604-21664: Marek Rogatko and Karol Wysokinski study massless Dirac fermions coupled to both ordinary electromagnetism and a dark photon sector, asking how a slightly uneven gravitational field alters transport. Working near flat spacetime, where the conformal transformation differs only slightly from Minkowski space, they avoid heavy curved-background quantum field theory. They find currents in both sectors tied to their beta functions. For a chargeless dark sector, they predict scale conductivity corrections that grow linearly in the dark sector and quadratically in the visible one.
arxiv-2604-21764: Zhao and five colleagues cut the cost of reasoning models by saving reusable reasoning skills instead of rethinking every problem from scratch. Their system distils skills from long deliberation and trial-and-error exploration, stores them, and recalls the relevant ones at inference time. That steers the model onto effective solution paths and away from redundant detours. On coding and maths reasoning tasks, the method uses far fewer reasoning tokens while improving overall performance.
arxiv-2604-21864: Sorrentino, Barbini, and Gatica-Perez review how AI adoption reshapes who holds power in newsrooms. Editorial authority means who decides, what counts as knowledge, and who answers for it. It moves inward as newsroom judgment defers to large language models built into newsroom work, through everyday, mental, and organisational habits that hide responsibility and weaken agency. It also moves outward to platforms, vendors, and infrastructure providers, widening power gaps. Participatory design is assessed as a way to keep or win back authority, with both promise and built-in limits.
arxiv-2604-21964: Barrett and six colleagues apply the Assurance 2.0 framework to externally review Google DeepMind's public scheming inability safety case. Safety cases should argue, with evidence, that harm risk stays within an acceptable bound. When developers author their safety cases, own bias and mixed motives can affect argument quality. External review can help address this. The review surfaces concerns affecting the scope of the safety case and its use in choices. The authors recommend how external review should be conducted and what information developers should provide.
arxiv-2604-22064: Flaminio, Inoue, and Kozhemiachenko study observations about chances, such as it rains 20% of the time, or rain and snow are equally likely. They put this problem in fuzzy probabilistic logic FP, and set out abduction problems and solutions. Their main work maps the complexity of spotting or finding fixes for an abduction problem in FP, for the full language and its or-clause parts.
arxiv-2604-22464: Qiu, Wu and Tan propose MADE-IT for ongoing model merging, joining task models into one design. Past methods face a saturation-redundancy dilemma: backbone methods fill limits, while expert-mixture types expand at random. MADE-IT grounds expert vectors in manifold geometry, using a subspace affinity metric and tuned threshold to guide expert evolution. It also uses a training-free implicit router turning on experts via feature-subspace match. Tests show MADE-IT beats strong rivals in accuracy and toughness across long and shuffled runs, while pruning spare experts.
arxiv-2604-22664: Howe and four colleagues evaluate which quantum circuits benefit from splitting into parts at two-qubit link points. Near-term hardware suffers high error rates, few qubits, and low quality, making large circuits difficult to run. Splitting promises a way around these limits, yet which circuit classes benefit most, and under what conditions, remains unclear. Fit is assessed for improving quality, enabling distributed runs, and scaling to circuit sizes. Uncut runs are compared against Qiskit's auto cut finding and a tuned cutting method across GHZ, QFT, brickwork, and random circuits.
arxiv-2604-22864: Achkar and four colleagues assemble Webis-SR4ALL-26, a corpus of 301,871 systematic reviews spanning all fields covered by OpenAlex. A staged pipeline links each review to metadata and reference lists. It also extracts reported search strategies and inclusion and exclusion criteria where authors state them. The layers support testing retrieval and screening, training extraction methods, and looking at review practice across fields. The team shows one use case with large-scale baseline retrieval signals.
arxiv-2604-22964: Patel presents AnemiaVision, a web-based system that screens for anemia without blood tests, using smartphone photos of the inner eyelid and fingernail beds. It fine-tunes an EfficientNet-B3 model with a new classifier head and training tricks including Mixup and wide augmentation. Early stopping follows peak validation accuracy, and the app keeps patient history across redeploys without data loss. It reaches 96.2 percent validation accuracy, far above a three-epoch CPU-only baseline, suiting it as a first-line screening tool for rural health workers.
arxiv-2604-23464: Dong and Li propose a design-based cross-validation method for judging small-area estimators. These tools fill in local health and development figures where survey data are thin. Their score rests on a decomposition of estimation error, with a bound on an unidentifiable bias serving as a ranking threshold. They also show a popular leave-one-area-out shortcut targets the wrong error and can flip the ranking. They apply the method to female literacy estimates in Zambia.
arxiv-2604-23564: Park and Kogiso design encrypted control systems that stay secure against attackers trying to identify the system from its signals, using post-quantum encryption with keys that change over time. Their update rules refresh the private key and ciphertexts together within a learning-with-errors scheme, and they derive parameter conditions that guarantee correct decryption at every step. A numerical example confirms secure control against the considered attack.
arxiv-2604-23864: Moyart extends Bourgain's method for K-closedness from classic harmonic analysis to the semicommutative setting. He uses the semicommutative Calderón-Zygmund decomposition of Cadilhac, Conde-Alonso, and Parcet. As an application he regains Pisier's result about noncommutative Hardy spaces on the torus, and gives fresh interpolation findings for noncommutative Sobolev spaces on the torus.
arxiv-2604-24064: Aertssen and four colleagues extend model predictive contouring control, a proven method for cars, to tractor-semitrailers. These rigs are larger, the trailer cuts its own path, and reversing risks jackknifing, so the method weights tractor and trailer anchor points by scenario and holds all wheels inside road bounds. Simulations pass a representative logistics run forward and backward, and first tests on a full-scale prototype show the approach works in practice.
arxiv-2604-24264: Han and colleagues describe alert handling and plans for the Ground Wide Angle Camera Network. GWAC-N pairs ten wide-field core telescopes with two 60cm follow-up units to catch optical counterparts of SVOM gamma-ray bursts. Core array monitoring triggers rapid multi-band follow-up on alert, but coordinating many units by hand is impractical. Operations run through an integrated alert chain with scheduling and dispatch, using SVOM's Follow-up Coordinating Service and the network's Automatic Management system.
arxiv-2604-24364: Chen and six colleagues test whether companions orbiting in under 5 days protect white dwarfs from metal pollution. About 25 to 50 percent of white dwarfs show metal lines from accreted planetary debris. From 17 companion systems, white dwarfs with close companions show a metal-pollution fraction of 7.7 percent. That is suppressed nearly sixfold relative to single white dwarfs, at over 99 percent confidence. Wider companions show about 25 percent, comparable to single systems. N-body integrations show massive close-in companions clearing 80 to 90 percent of small-body contaminants.
arxiv-2604-24564: Wang and four colleagues tackle a weakness in systems that answer questions from retrieved text, images and other media: retrieved items may look relevant without truly supporting the answer. Their MEG score weighs retrieved evidence by high-value words that carry the answer's core meaning, and MEG-RAG trains a reranker to favor that evidence. Tests on the M2RAG benchmark show steadier accuracy and cross-model consistency than strong baselines.
arxiv-2604-25264: Zeng and six colleagues propose MARD, a multi-agent framework for Android malware detection. Traditional detection suffers concept drift and shallow features. Large language models reason with meaning, but processing raw code costs many tokens. MARD bridges LLM understanding and static analysis, treating analysis engines as on-demand tools for orchestration. Through a ReAct-based mechanism, MARD builds an interpretable chain for conviction. Without fine-tuning, MARD reaches an F1 score of 93.46 percent and generalizes across domains over up to five years. Analysis of one APK costs under ten cents.
arxiv-2604-25364: Pardo-Montero asks how serial versus parallel organ build shapes the FLASH effect under uneven doses. He works out FLASH dose two ways: an oxygen-loss model, and a dose-rate curve. Both take the FLASH shield as local. Harm odds use the Lyman-Kutcher-Burman model and a dose match, with volume parallel or serial. Both ways show FLASH sparing beats plain rays, more as volume shrinks. If the shield is local, sparing can hinge on build, most for serial organs hurt by big local doses.
arxiv-2604-25764: Donkiewicz and Gaul study how to filter Benders cuts in large optimization problems split into a master problem and scenario subproblems. Adding every cut makes the master problem grow fast, yet some cuts are never violated and need never be added. They test violation-based filtering, diversity-based filtering by clustering cuts, and a hybrid taking the most-violated cut per cluster. Each can add an aggregated cut preserving discarded information. On 149 flow instances, all informed strategies solved at least 125, against 91 unfiltered, and cut solve time by more than half.
arxiv-2604-25864: Chen and Clerk build multi-mode bosonic models that realize quantum limit cycles with continuous O(N) symmetry under coherent parametric driving. A perfect quantum limit cycle wants fully coherent driving and continuous symmetry for monochromatic radiation, two demands that seem at odds. Remarkably, the full dissipative steady state of their models is exactly solvable. The models display steady-state entanglement, reduced phase diffusion, and possible quantum limit tori. One mechanism explains how parametric driving enriches limit cycles with symmetry, on optical and superconducting platforms.
arxiv-2604-25964: Vu, Tran, and Ngo study the error between exact solutions and Euler-Maruyama approximations for stochastic differential equations driven by Lévy processes, which allow sudden jumps. They measure that error in temporal-spatial Hölder norms, a yardstick controlling roughness jointly in time and space rather than at isolated points. Pinning down a strong convergence rate in those norms would give users a precise guarantee on approximation quality across both dimensions.
arxiv-2604-26164: He and six colleagues report a platform that applies large, uniform, reversible uniaxial strain to two-dimensional materials. It overcomes past limits below about one and a half percent and poor repeatability on cycling or cooling. Using chromium sulfur bromide as a model, they reach uniform strain near four percent with negligible slippage and controlled linear strain gradients across tens of micrometres. It also works across three phases of transition-metal dichalcogenides, including a record strain above five percent in tungsten ditelluride with a cleanly separating vibrational mode.
arxiv-2604-26364: Benerecetti and four colleagues characterized first-order logic over infinite trees with hesitant tree automata. Two new automata classes capture exactly two branching-time temporal logics already known to match first-order logic on infinite trees. The match yields a natural normal form through a new fragment of a temporal logic. As a consequence, along each branch first-order logic expresses only safety or co-safety properties, a sharp boundary for first-order definability.
arxiv-2604-26764: Santilli proves a condition that is both needed and enough for a C1-hypersurface to have all parallel sets nowhere C1-regular. It follows that for a generic C1-regular convex body, all inner parallel bodies have nowhere C1-regular boundaries. The result pins down exactly when offset surfaces of such a hypersurface fail to stay once-differentiable at any point.
arxiv-2604-26864: Secchi, Trakhinin and Wang study the free-border problem for relativistic plasma-vacuum borders in two and three spaces. Plasma flow follows ideal magnetohydrodynamics, while vacuum fields follow Maxwell's laws, with both magnetic fields tangential to a border moving with the plasma. They pin down a stability rule and prove linear stability for three-dimensional cases, via energy estimates in anisotropic Sobolev spaces. They also prove local existence and uniqueness in two spaces, when plasma and vacuum fields never vanish at once on the initial border.
arxiv-2604-27064: Premnath and thirty-five colleagues confirm four transiting giant planets around early-M dwarfs from the GEMS survey: TOI-7189 b, TOI-7265B b, TOI-7393 b, and TOI-7394B b. Periods run about one to four days, masses about half to about twice Jupiter's, radii near Jupiter's. Three are Saturn-like in mass and density; TOI-7394B b is a dense super-Jupiter on a roughly one-day orbit. Three hosts are metal-rich; TOI-7393 is the most metal-poor GEMS host yet.
arxiv-2604-27264: Robol and Giorgini introduce self-evolving software agents that combine BDI reasoning with large language models. Self-run agents adapt to changing environments but stay bound to requirements, goals, and skills fixed at design time. Their BDI-LLM design adds an automated evolution module beside the reasoning loop. It draws new requirements out of experience and builds design and code updates. A prototype in a dynamic multi-agent environment discovers new goals and generates working behaviors from minimal prior knowledge.
arxiv-2604-27564: Kveton and Valko tackle face recognition with just one image per person, a hard problem because training data are tiny. They consider recognizing only one person, with no labeled data for anyone else, which lacks negative examples. Framing it as one-class classification, they propose and analyze a non-parametric model learned from one labeled image plus a stream of unlabeled data. On 43 people, their method recognizes faces 90 percent of the time at nearly zero false positives, beating their best baseline by more than 25 percent.
arxiv-2604-27964: Buraglio, Dvorak and Woltran bring the divide-and-conquer technique of splitting to assumption-based argumentation, a formalism for reasoning over debates. Earlier splitting worked on the graph form of a framework, but turning assumption frameworks into graphs can blow up exponentially and blunt the gain. Splitting the knowledge base itself, extended to a parametrised form, avoids that blow-up and keeps the method useful.
arxiv-2604-28164: Chen and colleagues compute, for the first time, next-to-next-to-leading order QCD corrections to deeply virtual pion production, a key channel for mapping the nucleon's three-dimensional structure. Working in the generalised Bjorken limit within collinear factorisation, they cover charged and neutral pion channels at leading twist. The two-loop corrections are positive and substantial, considerably improving agreement with Jefferson Lab data, and they also study transverse spin asymmetries at three facilities.
arxiv-2605-00364:
Jiawei Wu and Doudou Zhou refine machine unlearning, the craft of making a trained language model forget specific knowledge. Privacy, safety, and legal duties can all require such forgetting. Standard methods retrain on whole sequences, updating every token alike, even though only some tokens carry the knowledge targeted for removal. That bluntness adds noise and damages the model's other skills.

Their framework, TokenUnlearn, scores tokens by importance, mixing a masking-based knowledge signal with an entropy-based one. It then either unlearns only the highest-scoring tokens or weights each token's update by its score. Theory shows the selection improves the signal-to-noise ratio of the update. Across two forgetting benchmarks and three model designs, the token-level approach forgot more cleanly while preserving more of the model's remaining ability.
arxiv-2605-00964:
Lennard C. Froma and four co-authors test whether model size matters when people seek information with retrieval-augmented assistants. Much research chases benchmark scores, while real collaborative use is less studied. Their realistic multi-turn scenario reflects workplace settings where legislation compliance and safe handling of sensitive data matter. More than one hundred participants worked with assistants built on models of three sizes.

Human-AI teams beat model-only and model-plus-retrieval baselines by a significant margin, regardless of model size. Perceived usability and satisfaction, however, differed little across the three sizes. The authors argue for evaluating AI in actual multi-turn human interaction, measuring usability and satisfaction alongside accuracy, rather than relying on benchmarks alone.
arxiv-2605-01064:
Annabelle Canestraight and three co-authors extend stochastic cluster expansion to excited-state energies in strongly tied electronic systems. Excited states are hard because the many-body space grows exponentially and controlled active spaces are difficult to choose. Building on a ground-state framework, the authors express excitation gaps directly as a hierarchy of orbital-space cluster parts.

A minimal frontier chemical subspace is treated exactly, while the rest of the orbital environment is sampled stochastically. Tests on charge-transfer complexes and polyacenes give accurate singlet-triplet gaps that agree with full-system results. Convergence comes from low-order cluster terms, and the framework can be systematically improved, offering a controlled route to excited states.
arxiv-2605-01164:
Wenshuo Wang argues in an essay that language models should not yet get credit for explaining human decisions. Recent work treats accurate behavior forecasts, plausible reasons, and outcome-based reasoning traces as evidence that models explain why people decide as they do. Wang separates three claims with different burdens: predicting, rationale generation, and a true account of causes.

The evidence usually offered directly supports the first two claims, and sometimes hypothesis formation, but does not distinguish explanation from forecast-supporting rationalization. A bridge standard is proposed: stronger claims should specify explanatory targets, rule out weaker rationalizer options, use process or intervention-sensitive validation, and bound scope. A credit calibration principle follows: models should get credit only for the strongest claim their evidence warrants.
arxiv-2605-01364:
Ting-Yu Dai, Kingsley Nweye, Dev Niyogi, and Zoltan Nagy take a step toward a single pre-trained model that can predict indoor heat flow for many homes at once. Today each building tends to need its own tuned model, which slows smart heating and cooling control.

Their design is a physics-informed Transformer that bakes in heat rules, such as rate-of-change features and step-by-step numerical updates, inside a decoder-only frame. It also reads fixed traits of each home from its simulation file. On a set of 247 homes in three climate zones, one-step forecasts land within about three tenths of a degree. A model trained on as few as two homes still works on new homes and new climates with no extra tuning.
arxiv-2605-01664:
Fariba Afrin Irany and Sampson Akwafuo build a question-answering system for biomedical documents that must show its receipts. Retrieval-augmented generation grounds a language model in fetched evidence, but weak retrieval, poor ranking, or unchecked claims can each break the chain.

Their framework runs on a commercial cloud stack: documents are parsed, chunked, embedded, and indexed, then a hybrid search pulls candidate passages and a dedicated reranker promotes the most relevant. Answers are written only from the top evidence, under conservative prompting. A separate judge model then checks every factual claim in the answer against the retrieved passages. In a pilot of twenty-five healthcare queries, five hundred chunks were pulled and two hundred claims checked, and every claim was judged supported. The authors present the layered checks as the real contribution, at proof-of-concept scale.
arxiv-2605-01764:
Beniamin Goldys, Agus L Soenjaya, and Thanh Tran analyze a simulation scheme for Hall magnetohydrodynamics. That is the plasma model where the magnetic field drifts with the electron flow, adding a stiff, fiercely nonlinear term. Any honest scheme must also keep the magnetic field divergence-free, a hard constraint that sloppy methods quietly break.

The team work on a Voigt-regularized version of the system, a smoothed model of independent interest that stays well-posed, and build a mixed finite element method around it. Exterior calculus machinery enforces the divergence condition exactly, and a skew-symmetric, linearly implicit time step gives unconditional energy stability. They prove optimal convergence rates for the regularized problem and, harder, error estimates for the raw system, where the regularization does real work in the non-resistive regime.
